turns.content: Prove the odd-index identity using the recurrence F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{m-1}.
Let d=ceil(n/2). Select d required Fibonacci differences whose indices are odd, treating F_1=F_2 consistently.
Represent the selected differences as edge lengths between real numbers and prove that these d edges cannot contain a cycle, using the largest odd-index Fibonacci length.
Explain why acyclicity gives the lower bound |S|>=d+1.
Verify that consecutive selected elements differ by F_{2j-1}, while differences from F_0 supply the even-index Fibonacci numbers needed up to n.
Confirm that every required F_k for 2<=k<=n occurs as a difference of two elements of S.
Count the elements in the construction.
Combine the lower bound and construction to give the minimum possible size of S.
